item.title: NATO scrambles jets after drones from Russia crash in Latvia
item.description:
Two drones entered NATO member Latvia from Russian territory early Thursday morning and crashed in the eastern Latgale region, with one striking an oil storage facility in the city of Rēzekne about 40 kilometers from the Russian border, according to the Latvian army.

Latvia's Defence Minister Andris Spruds told national broadcaster LSM that the drones were "probably launched by Ukraine against targets in Russia," suggesting they may have veered off course — possibly due to electronic warfare jamming — before entering Latvian airspace. No casualties were reported.

item.title: Trump hosts Lula at White House for tariff, minerals talks
item.description: President Donald Trump is welcoming Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to the White House on Thursday for a working meeting that spans tariffs, organized crime cooperation, and access to Brazil's vast rare earth mineral reserves. The encounter marks the first in-person bilateral meeting on American soil since Trump returned to office and the most consequential diplomatic moment of Lula's third term.

item.title: Russia tells diplomats to evacuate Kyiv ahead of May 9
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry on Wednesday issued a formal warning to all foreign diplomatic missions and international organizations in Kyiv, urging them to evacuate personnel ahead of possible large-scale strikes on the Ukrainian capital tied to the May 9 Victory Day commemorations.

item.title: Rubio meets Pope Leo XIV amid Trump-Vatican feud
item.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Rome on Thursday for a high-stakes diplomatic visit aimed at easing weeks of tension between the Trump administration, the Vatican, and the Italian government. Rubio is scheduled to meet Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican's Apostolic Palace on the morning of May 7, followed by meetings on Friday with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani.

The visit amounts to a diplomatic cleanup mission after President Donald Trump's escalating feud with the first American-born pope rattled relations with two of Washington's most important partners in Europe.

item.title: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait restore U.S. military base access after Hormuz standoff
item.description: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have lifted restrictions on U.S. military use of their bases and airspace, according to The Wall Street Journal, removing a major obstacle that had forced President Donald Trump to suspend his "Project Freedom" naval escort operation in the Strait of Hormuz just days ago.

item.title: Iran reviews US peace memo as Trump threatens bombing
item.description:
Iran said on Wednesday it is still reviewing a US peace proposal that could bring the war to an end, even as President Donald Trump renewed threats of military action against the Islamic Republic if a deal is not reached.

An Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson told the Iranian Students' News Agency (ISNA) that "the American proposal is still under examination by Iran, and once it is finalized, it will convey its opinion to the Pakistani side," referring to Pakistan's role as mediator in the negotiations.

Trump, speaking from the Oval Office, struck an optimistic tone: "They want to make a deal. We've had very good talks over the last 24 hours, and it's very possible that we'll make a deal". But hours later, he issued a stark warning on Truth Social: "If they don't agree, the bombing starts, and it will be, sadly, at a much higher level and intensity than it was before".

item.title: Trump gives EU until July 4 to ratify trade deal
item.description: President Donald Trump on Thursday issued a new ultimatum to the European Union, giving the bloc until July 4 — the 250th anniversary of American independence — to ratify a trade framework agreed last summer or face escalated tariffs. The announcement came after a phone call with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and hours after EU negotiators failed to reach a breakthrough in overnight talks on the deal's implementing legislation.

item.title: US strikes Iran after warships attacked in Hormuz
item.description: The United States and Iran exchanged fire on Thursday as three U.S. Navy destroyers transited the Strait of Hormuz, marking the most serious escalation since the two countries agreed to a ceasefire on April 8. U.S. Central Command said it intercepted the Iranian attacks and struck back at military facilities inside Iran, while President Trump dismissed the retaliatory strikes as a "love tap" and insisted the ceasefire remained intact.

item.title: Venice Biennale hit by mass protests, historic strike planned for Friday
item.description: The 61st Venice Biennale has plunged into political crisis during its opening week, with mass protests, a jury walkout, and a funding cut by the European Union transforming the world's most prestigious art exhibition into a battleground over the participation of Russia and Israel.

item.title: Kremlin drafts plan to sell peace deal as victory, leaked documents show
item.description: Internal documents from Russia's Presidential Administration reveal the Kremlin has been developing a propaganda strategy since late winter 2026 to frame a potential negotiated end to the war in Ukraine as a Russian victory, according to an investigation published by the Dossier Center this week.

item.title: Iran warns UAE will 'pay the price' after Qeshm blasts
item.description: Explosions rocked Iran's Qeshm Island and the port city of Bandar Abbas on Thursday night, prompting Iranian state-affiliated media to accuse the United Arab Emirates of carrying out a hostile action and warn that Abu Dhabi would face consequences if its involvement is confirmed.

item.title: Reform UK surges as Labour loses hundreds of seats in local elections
item.description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed he would "not walk away" on Friday as early results from England's local elections revealed a punishing night for the Labour Party, with Nigel Farage's Reform UK making dramatic gains across the country's traditional Labour heartlands.

item.title: Taiwan passes $25B defense bill for US arms purchases
item.description: Taiwan's legislature on Friday passed a NT$780 billion ($24.8 billion) special defense spending bill to fund purchases of American weapons, ending months of partisan gridlock over the island's military preparedness against China — but delivering far less than President Lai Ching-te's government had sought.

item.title: Trump-Xi summit proceeds despite Iran ceasefire strains
item.description: President Donald Trump is pressing ahead with plans to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing next week, even as a fragile ceasefire with Iran threatens to unravel and Chinese officials harbor reservations about the timing of the high-stakes encounter.

item.title: US fires on two more Iranian tankers breaching blockade
item.description:
The US military fired on and disabled two Iranian-flagged oil tankers on Friday that were attempting to violate the ongoing American naval blockade of Iran's ports, escalating tensions even as Washington awaits Tehran's response to a proposed deal to end the two-month war.

The strikes came two days after US forces disabled a third tanker, the M/T Hasna, on Wednesday by firing 20mm cannon rounds from an F/A-18 Super Hornet to knock out the vessel's rudder as it ignored warnings to stop in the Gulf of Oman, according to US Central Command.

item.title: Satellite images reveal massive oil spill near Iran's Kharg Island
item.description: Satellite imagery has revealed a large oil spill spreading across dozens of square kilometers of sea near Iran's Kharg Island, the country's primary crude export terminal, as the U.S. naval blockade continues to choke Tehran's oil trade and push its storage capacity toward its limits.

item.title: Iran's FM says missile arsenal grew despite US strikes
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Friday dismissed a U.S. intelligence assessment that Iran's missile capabilities had been degraded by months of American and Israeli strikes, claiming Tehran's arsenal has actually grown since the war began and declaring Iran "1,000% ready" to defend itself.

item.title: Rubio calls Iran's claim over Strait of Hormuz 'unacceptable' as U.S. awaits deal response
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared on Friday that Iran's effort to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz was "unacceptable," warning from Rome that the international community must be prepared to respond with "more than strongly worded statements" to push back against Tehran's claims over the critical waterway.

item.title: Trump announces three-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire with prisoner swap
item.description: President Donald Trump announced on Thursday a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, declaring on Truth Social that the pause will include a suspension of all kinetic activity and a prisoner exchange of 1,000 individuals from each country. The announcement came as both sides were already trading accusations of violating earlier, competing unilateral truces declared in the lead-up to Russia's Victory Day celebrations on May 9.

item.title: US intel says Iran's Khamenei shaping war strategy
item.description: Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is playing a key role in shaping Tehran's war strategy and negotiations with the United States despite remaining out of public view for more than two months, according to a U.S. intelligence assessment reported by CNN on Thursday. The assessment comes as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian confirmed he recently met with Khamenei in person, easing weeks of speculation about whether the wounded leader was capable of governing.
